title: Getting started with orbis
text: plot starts data mapping variables visual channels. Layers added +. Recognised channels x, y, colour (color), fill, size, label, group tooltip. mapping given inside layer applies layer . Continuous variables mapped colour use perceptually uniform ramp; character factor variables get qualitative palette interactive legend.
code: p <- orb(mtcars, x = wt, y = mpg, colour = hp, size = disp) +   orb_points() +   orb_labs(title = "Fuel economy", x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",            y = "Miles per gallon", colour = "Horsepower") p orb(mtcars, x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl)) +   orb_points() +   orb_theme_dark()

title: Getting started with orbis
text: orb_bars() accepts discrete x:
code: set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(t = 1:80, v = cumsum(rnorm(80, 0.05)))  orb(df, x = t, y = v) +   orb_area(alpha = 0.3) +   orb_line(width = 2, smooth = TRUE) +   orb_labs(title = "A smoothed series") counts <- data.frame(g = c("alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta"),                      v = c(23, 41, 17, 35)) orb(counts, x = g, y = v, fill = g) +   orb_bars() +   orb_options(legend = FALSE, grid = "y") +   orb_theme_ink()

title: Getting started with orbis
text: orb_facet() draws one panel per level variable. Panels share scales default, makes comparable glance. Use scales = "free" ("free_x", "free_y") panels cover different ranges, ncol control grid: Colours sizes resolved across whole data set rather per panel, colour means thing everywhere.
code: orb(mtcars, x = wt, y = mpg, colour = hp) +   orb_points() +   orb_facet(cyl) +   orb_labs(title = "By cylinder count", x = "Weight", y = "MPG") set.seed(3) d <- data.frame(t = rep(1:40, 3),                 v = c(cumsum(rnorm(40)), cumsum(rnorm(40, 0.3)),                       cumsum(rnorm(40, -0.2))),                 region = rep(c("north", "south", "east"), each = 40)) orb(d, x = t, y = v) +   orb_area(alpha = 0.3) + orb_line() +   orb_facet(region, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y")

title: Getting started with orbis
text: Scales set palettes, limits axis transformations. Available palettes:
code: orb(mtcars, x = wt, y = mpg, colour = hp) +   orb_points() +   orb_scale_colour("magma", reverse = TRUE) +   orb_scale_size(range = c(3, 16)) +   orb_scale_y(limits = c(10, 35)) orb_palettes() #> $continuous #> [1] "viridis"  "magma"    "mako"     "ember"    "ice"      "spectral" "balance"  #>  #> $discrete #> [1] "orbis" "vivid" "earth" "neon"

title: Getting started with orbis
text: simplified world dataset ships package. orb_worldmap() quickest way map. Supply values shade regions variable. Six projections built . equalearth good modern default thematic maps: equal-area, shaded country sizes directly comparable, keeping continents close familiar shapes. orthographic projection draws globe hides hemisphere facing away viewer. Points placed active projection orb_geo_points():
code: str(world_map) #> 'data.frame':    26953 obs. of  4 variables: #>  $ long  : num  -69.9 -70.1 -70 -69.9 74.9 ... #>  $ lat   : num  12.5 12.5 12.6 12.5 37.2 ... #>  $ group : int  1 1 1 1 2 2 2 2 2 2 ... #>  $ region: chr  "Aruba" "Aruba" "Aruba" "Aruba" ... vals <- data.frame(region = c("Brazil", "India", "France", "China", "Nigeria"),                    v = c(3, 9, 5, 8, 6)) orb_worldmap(values = vals, value_col = "v", projection = "robinson") +   orb_labs(title = "A small choropleth") orb_worldmap(values = vals, value_col = "v", projection = "equalearth",              palette = "ice") +   orb_labs(title = "Equal Earth") orb_worldmap(projection = "orthographic", ocean = "#0B1F33") +   orb_coord_map("orthographic", centre = c(20, 15)) +   orb_theme_dark() cities <- data.frame(   long = c(2.35, -74.0, 151.2, 77.2, -43.2),   lat  = c(48.86, 40.7, -33.87, 28.6, -22.9),   pop  = c(11, 19, 5, 32, 13) ) orb(cities, x = long, y = lat, size = pop) +   orb_map(fill = "#E9ECEF") +   orb_geo_points(colour = "#F76707") +   orb_coord_map("robinson") +   orb_labs(title = "Cities")

title: Getting started with orbis
text: One plot object, several destinations. format follows file extension. Raster output laid width x height logical pixels rendered requested dpi, 300 600 dpi figure keeps proportions saw screen. interactive output supports: hovering mark tooltip, scrolling zoom dragging pan, double-clicking reset view, clicking legend key hide show series. Set orb_options(interactive = FALSE) document must contain scripts.
code: orb_save(p, "figure.png", dpi = 600)   # high-resolution raster for print orb_save(p, "figure.pdf")              # vector orb_save(p, "figure.svg")              # vector, still interactive orb_save(p, "figure.html")             # self-contained interactive page orb_interactive(p)                     # open in the viewer

title: Map projections — orb_coord_map
text: object class orb_coord, added plot.

title: Map projections — orb_coord_map
text: Available projections: equirectangular Longitude latitude used directly; simple fast, distorts area away equator. mercator Conformal cylindrical projection; preserves angles, greatly exaggerates high latitudes. Latitudes clipped \(\pm\)max_lat. robinson compromise projection widely used world maps. mollweide Equal-area pseudo-cylindrical projection. equalearth Equal Earth projection Savric, Patterson Jenny (2019): equal-area, like Mollweide, continents shaped much closer familiar Robinson outline. good modern default thematic world maps, areas distorted. orthographic view globe infinite distance, centred centre; hemisphere facing away viewer hidden.

title: orbis 0.1.0
text: First release. layered grammar (orb() plus +) compiles resolution-independent scene description, rendered either interactive SVG R’s graphics devices resolution. Layers: orb_points(), orb_line(), orb_bars(), orb_area(), orb_text(). Faceting orb_facet(), shared free scales. Geography built : orb_map(), orb_geo_points(), orb_worldmap(), world_map dataset, six projections via orb_coord_map(), including equal-area Equal Earth projection orthographic globe. Scales, four themes perceptually uniform palettes. Output orb_save() (SVG, HTML, PDF, PNG, TIFF, JPEG), orb_svg(), orb_interactive() orb_draw().
